elements.element: Vendor must have a duty to defend covered claims.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) states that Contractor shall “defend” against the covered claims.

elements.element: Vendor must have a duty to indemnify against losses resulting from covered claims.
elements.evidence: Contractor must “indemnify and hold harmless” from claims and all resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: The protected indemnitees must include Customer and Customer’s affiliates.
elements.evidence: The duties expressly protect “Company and its affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d)(i) covers allegations that the “Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d)(ii) covers “Contractor’s breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include data breaches caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d)(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company data or Confidential Information caused by Contractor.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d)(iv) expressly covers Contractor’s gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide notice of the claim.
elements.evidence: Company must provide Contractor with prompt written notice.

elements.element: Vendor must control the defence of covered claims.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Contractor shall control the defence, subject to a settlement-consent restriction.

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defence.
elements.evidence: Company must provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor’s expense.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no indemnification obligation on Company. The condition for limiting a Customer indemnity is therefore demonstrably absent; the heading alone does not create an operative obligation.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d)(i) provides an express Contractor indemnity for third-party allegations that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Company appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude claims resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Company specifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to procure continued rights to use the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no procurement-of-rights remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to modify the affected services or deliverables to become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to replace the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must provide a refund if the other infringement remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No operative language shown applies a 3× annual-fees cap to Contractor’s indemnification liability.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred Vendor indemnity, including the four required triggers, Customer and affiliate protection, defence and indemnification duties, and notice/control/cooperation procedures. The absence of any operative Customer indemnity satisfies the limitation on such an obligation conditionally. The attorneys’ fee carveout is directly related and prevents the existing waiver from neutralizing indemnified defence costs. The fallback is not independently complete because it lacks the specified IP exclusions, infringement remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap.
